# Reference fixtures

Pinned here and **never re-fetched at test time.** A test that downloads its own
reference can fail because a server changed, and can silently begin validating
against different coordinates — which is worse, because it still passes.

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` §11 for the required steps when adding one. The third step
is the one that is easy to skip and expensive to skip: assert that the reference
output was computed on the coordinates committed beside it.

| File                   | What it is                                  | Source                                          | Retrieved   |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `1crn.pdb`             | Crambin, 46 residues, no ligand             | `https://files.rcsb.org/download/1CRN.pdb`      | 2026-08-16  |
| `1crn.dssp`            | DSSP output for the above                   | `https://pdb-redo.eu/dssp/db/1crn/legacy`       | 2026-08-16  |
| `1btl.pdb`             | TEM-1 beta-lactamase, 263 residues, SO4     | `https://files.rcsb.org/download/1BTL.pdb`      | 2026-08-16  |
| `1btl.dssp`            | DSSP output for the above                   | `https://pdb-redo.eu/dssp/db/1btl/legacy`       | 2026-08-16  |
| `1btl_golden_sasa.csv` | Our own per-residue ASA/RSA/region for 1BTL | generated by `codonlab.features.structure`      | 2026-08-16  |

DSSP version: 4.6.1 (NKI), per the header line in each `.dssp` file.

## Why two kinds of reference

`1crn.dssp` and `1btl.dssp` are **independent** references: someone else's
implementation, so they validate our absolute numbers.

`1btl_golden_sasa.csv` is **our own** output, so it validates nothing on its own —
it pins the parameters. Both are needed, because agreement with DSSP does not
discriminate the van der Waals radii set: a uniform-radius model correlates with
DSSP at r = 0.998 while moving 8 of 1BTL's 263 residues across a region boundary.
`ARCHITECTURE.md` §13 generalises that finding into a standing rule.

Regenerate the golden file only when a parameter change is *intended*, and say so
in the commit message. If it changes without one, that is the test working.

## Coordinate check

Both DSSP files were confirmed to have been computed on the committed PDB files by
comparing the CA coordinates DSSP prints against the coordinate records: maximum
deviation 0.0 Å for 1CRN and 0.1 Å for 1BTL, which is DSSP's one-decimal print
precision. `tests/test_sasa.py` re-asserts this on every run.

**That result will not hold in general.** A re-refined structure has genuinely
different coordinates from the deposited entry. If a future fixture fails this
check, the fixture is mismatched — do not widen the tolerance.
